title: Defer per-request randomness under Cache Components
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/request-id/page.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Confirm the fallback/static shell behavior and avoid displaying telemetry secrets.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: When the requirement is a new value per request, defer the operation to runtime and contain it with a Suspense boundary in the Cache Components model.
alternativeApproaches: No. It is useful for measuring a duration, not a durable or globally unique request identity. Keep timing telemetry out of rendered content unless the UI requirement explicitly needs it.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Confirm the fallback/static shell behavior and avoid displaying telemetry secrets.
nextjsPractice.next15: This stable API is a Next.js 16 exercise. Do not copy it into a 15 project; design a version-appropriate alternative and verify patch-specific types.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
